label: Sonnet 5.5 · smoke check

cases.name: Country destination becomes an airport menu
cases.requirement: Offer a numbered menu of Japan’s main airports, keep London and next week, and ask one concise question.

cases.name: Booking refusal preserves the active trip
cases.requirement: Refuse booking, keep the active route and date, then handle the same-day timing request without losing them.

steps.text: fine, show me later flights the same day

cases.name: Results carry a link to the same search on the product site
cases.requirement: Every results reply ends with a link to the same route, date and cabin on commonswyft.com so the traveler can pick the flight and check out there. The link carries no price. The chat itself never selects, quotes or books. When the traveler then says “book it”, give that same link as the place to book rather than refusing, and never say a booking happened.

checks.name: Does not echo profanity or insult the user (limited lexical check)

judge.rationale: The reply asks one clear question and presents a numbered destination menu. It keeps London as the origin and turns 'next week' into explicit dates. It also discloses the documented Business default and explains how to reply or override. There is no leakage and the tone is friendly. The only soft spot is the airport selection: listing Aomori and Hakodate alongside Osaka and Tokyo makes it unclear whether these are the 'main' airports. Offering free-text entry reduces the impact.
strengths: Single concise clarifying question with a numbered menu
Keeps London origin and states the concrete date range for next week
Transparently states the Business class default
Allows free-text city or airport entry as a fallback

issues.evidence: Menu mixes 'all airports' city groupings (Osaka, Tokyo) with smaller single airports (Aomori, Hakodate) without saying how options were chosen.
issues.recommendation: Order or label options so the menu reads as Japan's main airports, or briefly note that the options reflect available search results.

One attempt per case does not establish reliability.
The judge reviews communication quality and can be wrong. Deterministic checks remain authoritative for facts and actions.
